name: United Microelectronics Corporation
business_model: Contract wafer foundry; incorporated 1980 as an ITRI spin-off and later switched from IDM to pure-play foundry (see CLM-0104, CLM-0105).

name: Chartered Semiconductor Manufacturing Ltd.
business_model: Singapore wafer foundry (historical); majority-owned by ST Semiconductors, acquired by an ATIC affiliate in December 2009 and combined with GLOBALFOUNDRIES in 2010.

name: GLOBALFOUNDRIES Inc.
business_model: Specialty/mature-node contract foundry formed in 2009 from AMD's manufacturing operations; added Chartered (2010) and IBM Microelectronics (2015). Incorporated in the Cayman Islands; principal offices in Malta, New York.

name: Xilinx, Inc.
business_model: Fabless FPGA/programmable-logic company founded in 1984; bought wafers from Seiko (first), later UMC and TSMC (historical).

name: Lattice Semiconductor Corporation
business_model: Fabless programmable-logic company (incorporated in Oregon 1983); sources wafers from foundry partners and assembly from Asian subcontractors.

name: Chips and Technologies, Inc.
business_model: Early fabless PC chipset company (mid-1980s, historical); used Toshiba gate arrays and Hitachi bipolar fabrication.

name: Synopsys, Inc.
business_model: EDA software (time-based licences) and design-IP licensing; incorporated 1986 in North Carolina.

name: Mentor Graphics Corporation
business_model: EDA vendor incorporated in Oregon in 1981 (historical); later part of Siemens (Siemens EDA is named by Synopsys as a competitor, CLM-0494).

name: Rambus Inc.
business_model: Memory-interface chips plus patent and technology licensing (see CLM-2008, CLM-2009).

name: LSI Logic Corporation
business_model: ASIC/storage chip company that adopted a fabless model in 2005 and sold its Gresham fab in 2006 (historical); later part of Avago (per IC Insights).

name: ON Semiconductor Corporation
business_model: IDM (power, analog); bought LSI's Gresham fab in 2006 to expand in-house manufacturing.

name: Texas Instruments Incorporated
business_model: Analog and embedded-processing IDM; in 2007 stopped in-house advanced digital process development in favour of foundry partners while keeping its own fabs.

name: Infineon Technologies AG
business_model: IDM carved out of Siemens (stand-alone from 1 April 1999); 'fab-light' from c.2007, outsourcing advanced logic to foundries.

name: Freescale Semiconductor, Inc.
business_model: Former Motorola semiconductor operations, spun off by 2 December 2004 (historical).

name: NXP Semiconductors N.V.
business_model: Former Philips Semiconductors; 80.1% sold to a private-equity consortium in September 2006 and renamed NXP.
